# Edit in Premiere

Premiere owns `.prproj` and edits to its sequences. An FCP 7 `.xml` or `.aaf`
timeline opens in Premiere; it can't import `.fcpxml` directly (FCP 7 `.xml` is
a different format it can) and imports `.otio` only from version 25.6.

When choosing takes, lines or cut points from footage, follow [local footage review](../edit-video/SKILL.md#review-footage-locally) first.

Make a new cut as a Premiere XML (FCP7) timeline with every clip linked and titles
as text; Voyager has no FCP7 XML writer, so write it yourself. When Premiere is open,
import it into the open project yourself with File > Import, then check media links,
track layout, timing and that titles are still editable text.

Change an existing sequence (titles, fades, music, markers) in place, never by
rebuilding it: use computer tools, or close the project in Premiere, edit the
`.prproj` (gzipped XML) and reopen it. Premiere overwrites a file changed while it is
open. Copy the `.prproj` before editing it, and keep the original if the reopened edit
is wrong. Make titles Premiere text, not rendered images.

Use Voyager computer tools for export, effects, ripple edits or UI review.
